(ICTSI)’s container terminal in Poland to handle the largest vessel to call the Gdynia port. ICTSI said that Baltic Container Terminal (BCT) successfully handled the inaugural call of MSC Venice – the largest and longest vessel to call at the Port of Gdynia. The 399-meter-long vessel with a capacity of 16,652 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) recently docked at BCT, demonstrating the port’s capability to service the largest container ships operating in the Baltic Sea. “The arrival of MSC Venice is a defining moment for BCT and the Port of Gdynia. It validates the significant investments made by all stakeholders to accommodate the next generation of larger container ships and reinforces our position as a deep-water gateway port to support Poland’s economic growth,” BCT chief executive officer Patrick Chan said. Recent upgrades in BCT include the commissioning of new quay cranes and yard equipment. ICTSI said these investments have significantly expanded the terminal’s operational capabilities and capacity to efficiently handle the largest container vessels in the Baltic Sea. It said the successful call is likewise a result of years of cooperation with and commitment from numerous partners and all stakeholders involved in the development of the port. BCT at the Port of Gdynia is a leading container terminal in Poland. As one of the largest and most modern marine terminals in the Baltic region, BCT has a capacity of over a million TEUs. The terminal is strategically located within pan-European corridor and railway routes, offering excellent truck and on-dock rail connectivity to Europe’s hinterlands. https://verticalmag.com/press-releases/a.text: Photo Info Aviation Specialties Unlimited hires Jakub Dryska as new territory manager Aviation Specialties Unlimited Press Release | September 3, 2026 Estimated reading time 2 minutes, 51 seconds. Jakub Dryska. ASU Photo Aviation Specialties Unlimited (ASU), a provider of night vision solutions, announced that Jakub Dryska was hired as the company’s new territory manager for Europe and Africa. Dryska replaces Alexander Emmel, who was recently promoted to ASU’s director of international sales. “Jakub brings with him more than a decade of international aviation experience,” said Emmel. “He is well known and respected in the industry and throughout Europe.” As the new territory manager for Europe and Africa, Dryska will assist with international sales and business development. Prior to joining ASU, Dryska spent his career with AIR TEAM in the Czech Republic, where he progressed through several commercial leadership roles, including PART 145 sales manager, business development manager, and, most recently, director of key accounts. Dryska is from the Czech Republic and will operate from an office within the CET time zone. “Throughout my career, I have focused on developing long-term relationships with commercial, government, and defense aviation customers across Europe,” said Dryska. “My experience includes aircraft modernization projects, special mission aviation programs, NVG cockpit modifications, and managing complex business-to-business and business-to-government sales opportunities. I have also worked extensively with government tenders, NATO-related projects, and export compliance requirements, including ITAR training completed through the U.S. Embassy in Prague. I have built a strong professional network throughout Europe and look forward to expanding ASU’s presence across Europe and Africa.” “Because of his background, training, and experience in the Czech Republic, Jakub will be able to serve our customers in Europe and Africa with a depth of knowledge that is needed,” said Emmel. “We look forward to expanding our capabilities throughout Europe and Africa.” Emmel and Dryska will be at the upcoming MSPO Defense Industry Exhibition in Kielce, Poland, September 8-11, at stand 6-C01.
